messages:
sasha: Heads up — noticed a p50 latency regression after the kernel-selection change rolled this morning. 2k seq, batch=8, p50 went from ~120ms -> ~155ms on prod GPUs. Not huge but consistent across hosts.
ryan: ugh. did we flip fallback ordering? which kernel is being picked now?
marta: I saw that too on a few customer traces. looks like some requests are falling through to fused_flash_v2 instead of fused_flash_v1 for certain seq/bin combos.
sasha: confirmed. route shows fallback -> fused_flash_v2 for seq_len>=1024 and kv-cold. before it was fused_flash_v1.
lee: can we get a quick profile (nvprof / nsight)? might be a kernel launch / shared memory thing.
sasha: pasted a short perf diff: ```before: fused_flash_v1 p50=118ms, p95=420ms; after: fused_flash_v2 p50=153ms, p95=430ms``` CPU stacks show more memcpy in fallback path.
ryan: CI bisect suggestion: revert the kernel-selector predicate locally to force v1 and rerun smoke bench. @ci-bot can we run smoke/attn/2k-b8 on the canary pool? :eyes:
ci-bot: queued job attn-smoke/2k-b8/1719156799 on canary-pool-3. ETA ~6m.
perf-bot: quick flame summary (canary-pool-3): fused_flash_v2 shows 22% higher kernel time + larger kernel-launch overhead. KV access pattern the same.
marta: interesting — could be a small change in lane packing for v2. v2 has extra boundary checks for tiled loads (added for correctness on small seq).
lee: if it's checks on the hot loop, cost adds up for batch=8. try forcing batch=32 in the selector to see if the delta disappears.
sasha: I patched selector locally to prefer v1 for batch<=16 and reran local bench: p50 back to 121ms. Not perfect repro but points at selector logic.
ryan: bisect plan: 1) run canary with selector pinned to v1 (confirm regression goes away). 2) revert just the predicate commit and test. 3) if repro, add microbenchmark for the boundary check code path.
marta: I can add a tiny microbench that toggles the tiled-load path and measures per-token overhead. Will push in a PR to my fork.
sasha: for immediate mitigation I set rollout to 10% and added an autoswitch fallback to v1 when p50 > 140ms for a route. Rolling out now.
lee: thanks. keep an eye on p95 too. if launch overhead spikes we might still see tail regressions.
ryan: long-term: either fix the extra checks in fused_flash_v2 (opt them out for common sizes) or adjust selector heuristics to account for launch overhead at small batch sizes.
sasha: noted. assigning followups: @marta microbench, @lee kernel audit, @ryan update selector heuristics. I’ll watch canary metrics.
perf-bot: canary metrics: p50 -> back to 125ms after rollback to 10% config (within noise). p95 unchanged.
ci-bot: attn-smoke job completed: success. logs -> https://ci/internal/attn-smoke/1719156799
ryan: good. thanks all. we should capture this as a perf-debt item and add a short experiment to the sprint: "measure kernel launch vs compute tradeoff across batch sizes". :+1:
sasha: will file GH issue and link traces.
lee: FYI — added a quick note to the kernel guide about guarding tiled-load checks with a compile-time flag for the common path.
marta: PR with microbench linked in that issue shortly.
sasha: cool. closing the noisy alert, will re-open if canary worsens. :white_check_mark:
